rem:frobenius-codim-universal-interpreta:
Remark Physical content: the tower residual as \tau(C_{\dim_q}). Physical content. Any vortex on the self-dual Frobenius algebra inherits a tower residual. The residual equals the trace of the quantum-co-dimension element scaled by the electron mass m_e:

  \Delta m_{\text{vortex}}
  \;=\;
  m_e \cdot \tau\bigl(C_{\dim_q}^{(A)}\bigr).

Whether a proton tower residual equals this quantity is the comparison recorded in proton tower residual vs m_e\sum_\lambda 1/\dim_q\lambda; no derivation of the residual is claimed. The quantity is not the Markov trace of the Frobenius Casimir of H_3(q) (Frobenius Casimir of H_3(q)).

What the theorem does and does not supply. The identity is a consequence of semisimplicity, not an independent constraint. The element C_{\dim_q} is constructed so that its trace is \sum_\lambda 1/\dim_q(\lambda); once the central idempotents p_\lambda exist with \tau(p_\lambda) and \dim_q(\lambda) invertible, linearity of \tau over that basis gives the identity with nothing further to check. The word universal in the title records that the argument uses no property of A beyond being a semisimple Frobenius algebra with a trace — it does not record a discovery about A.

The content therefore sits in the hypothesis rather than the conclusion. What is being asserted about a quantum universe is that its aether has channels at all: the Wedderburn semisimplicity axiom supplies the finite block set, the non-vanishing Frobenius weights, and the invertible quantum dimensions. Given those, the co-Casimir trace follows. Read the other way round — as though the numerical identity constrained the algebra — it would be circular.
rem:np-discrepancy-resolution:
Remark n/p discrepancy resolution: calibration-dependent, not structural. The uncalibrated pure-tower formula undershoots the neutron mass due to a \Phi_q pole-distance asymmetry. The free-neutron beta decay prediction must instead use the trace difference directly.

The raw tower prediction relies on per-generator amplitudes that sit at different distances from the q_0 pole. This introduces an artificial scale difference between mirror nucleons. Bypassing the per-nucleon evaluation entirely, the uncalibrated beta-decay Q-value emerges directly from the difference of the Markov normal forms:

  \mathfrak{Q}_\beta = \bigl|\mathrm{tr}_M(\Delta)\bigr| \cdot E_0 \approx 0.4491\;\mathrm{MeV},

evaluated with the canonical Markov trace at z = q_0^3/(q_0^2+1). Here E_0 = m_e/\bigl(q_0(q_0-1)(1-\hbar_q^2)\bigr) is the tower-summed energy scale, with \hbar_q = 1 - q_0^{-1}; the order-zero form gives 0.4447 MeV. This misses CODATA by -42.59\% (-333.2 keV); the c_k ladder that would correct it at z = q^3/(q^2+1) has not been derived. The scored value is not the \Delta trace. It applies the T^3 weight split of the same z = q_0^3/(q_0^2+1) trace to the \gamma\gamma base V^3 = (\sigma_0\sigma_1^{-1})^3 and gives \mathfrak{Q}_\beta \approx 0.3254 MeV (-58.40\%) (Symbolic Q-value of free neutron decay). The \Delta value is kept as an unscored comparison. It relies on the topological trace alone, avoiding the single-generator Kashaev approximations. The retired Form A, which weights every basis element by 1 (the trace at z = 1, not a two-row Markov trace), gave 0.7836 MeV, within 1.3 keV of CODATA; it is kept only as a historical cross-check.
prop:pair-graph-regime-trichotomy:
Proposition Pair-graph regimes of A: 2\bigl(\binom A2-(3A-6)\bigr)=(A-3)(A-4) splits A\ge2 into \{2\}, \{3,4\}, \{\ge5\}. For A\ge2 let K_A be the complete graph on A vertices. Define the pair-graph regime of A by

r(A)=\begin{cases}
\mathrm{I} & \binom A3 = 0,\\
\mathrm{II} & \binom A3>0 \text{ and } \binom A2\le 3A-6,\\
\mathrm{III} & \binom A2 > 3A-6.
\end{cases}

Here \binom A3=0 says that K_A has no triangle, and 3A-6 is the number of edges of a triangulated 2-sphere on A vertices. Then, for every natural number A,

2\Bigl(\tbinom A2-(3A-6)\Bigr)=(A-3)(A-4),

and for A\ge2 exactly one of the following holds:

  1. A=2, so r(A)=\mathrm I;
  2. A\in\{3,4\}, with \binom A2 = 3A-6, so r(A)=\mathrm{II};
  3. A\ge5, with \binom A2>3A-6, so r(A)=\mathrm{III}.

In particular the deltahedral max-contact count \kappa(A) (\kappa(2)=1, \kappa(A)=3A-6 for A\ge3) equals \binom A2 if and only if A\le4.

The statement is integer arithmetic.

Geometrically (classical, not used above): for A\ge3, \binom A2\le3A-6 says K_A is the 1-skeleton of a triangulated 2-sphere (the doubled triangle at A=3, the tetrahedron at A=4); for A\ge5, K_A\supseteq K_5 is not planar. Equivalently, A equal spheres in \mathbb{R}^3 can be pairwise tangent if and only if A\le4.
prf:pair-graph-regime-trichotomy:
Proof Proof of the pair-graph regime trichotomy. By Pascal's rule \binom{n+1}2 = n+\binom n2, so by induction 2\binom A2 = A(A-1) in \mathbb Z. Hence

2\tbinom A2-2(3A-6) = A^2-7A+12 = (A-3)(A-4).

The right side is 0 at A=3,4 and at least 2 for A\ge5, so \binom A2=3A-6 for A\in\{3,4\} and \binom A2>3A-6 for A\ge5. Also \binom A3=0 if and only if A<3. For A\ge2 the cases A=2, A\in\{3,4\} and A\ge5 are exhaustive and disjoint, which gives the trichotomy. For \kappa: \kappa(2)=1=\binom22, \kappa(3)=3=\binom32, \kappa(4)=6=\binom42, and \kappa(A)=3A-6<\binom A2 for A\ge5.

\blacksquare
conj:mass-formula-regime-switching:
Conjecture Mass formula regime switch: an A-uniform evaluation whose dominant term changes at the pair-graph regime boundaries A = 2 \mid 3 and 4 \mid 5. There is a single evaluation of the binding energy B(Z,N) that does not branch on A, whose dominant contribution changes character exactly at the boundaries of the pair-graph regimes r(A) of Pair-graph regimes of A: regime I (A=2), regime II (A\in\{3,4\}) and regime III (A\ge5). The piecewise evaluation

  B(Z, N)
  \;=\;
  \begin{cases}
    B_{\mathrm{SW}}(Z, N) + m_e\,\tau(C_{\dim_q}^{H_3})
      & \text{if } A = 2, \\[4pt]
    B_{\mathrm{BW}+\chi}(Z, N)
      & \text{if } 3 \leq A \leq 4, \\[4pt]
    B_{\mathrm{BW}}(Z, N) + B_{\mathrm{shell}}(A)
      & \text{if } A \geq 5
  \end{cases}

is then a description of that change, not a definition of B.

What is proved is only where the boundaries fall: by Pair-graph regimes of A, 2\bigl(\binom A2-(3A-6)\bigr)=(A-3)(A-4), so the cut-offs 2\mid3 and 4\mid5 depend on A alone. That criterion was identified after the cut-offs below had been selected. No result derives which evaluation belongs to which regime, and no A-uniform evaluation with this property has been established.

The earlier description of the regimes as "non-additive", because the Schur–Weyl and Bethe–Weizsäcker evaluations would count overlapping Wedderburn content, is not a well-posed statement: B_{\mathrm{BW}+\chi} is a polynomial in A and Z with q-integer coefficients, not a sum over Wedderburn blocks, so there is no common index set on which an overlap could be shown or refuted.

Comparison (selection against the measured target; not a prediction). Table 2 lists, per isotope, the error of each evaluation against AME. The column marked regime-selected is chosen per isotope by the smaller AME deviation. This is post-hoc selection against the target—one discrete choice per branch—and therefore constitutes fitting. The statement that the selected regime agrees with AME to within 5\% for A\le4 uses a tolerance sized to its own largest miss (^4He, -4.07\%). The chirality factors in B_{\mathrm{BW}+\chi} are assigned per isotope by hand. The readings "the Schur–Weyl evaluation applies to the light satellite topology of the deuteron" and "collective Wedderburn states dominate for the Borromean topologies at A\ge3" are physical glosses without a definition of "dominate".

prose:intro-six-term-crystal-isospin-chi:
Assembling the volume leading term, the surface crossing deficiency, the Coulomb topological charge pairing, the Wigner Jucys–Murphy symmetry energy, the pairing parity step, and the Plancherel shell residue produces the complete six-term categorical mass formula. Every phenomenological coefficient of the empirical Bethe–Weizsäcker liquid-drop model is thereby replaced by a closed algebraic invariant of the braid normal form in H_A(q).

This section states the complete six-term mass formula, derives its per-term Wedderburn weights, proves exact isospin degeneracy in the q \to 0 Kashiwara crystal limit, and demonstrates how electromagnetic localization on the canonical bowtie interface breaks crystal isospin at q_0.

\begin{aligned}
  B(Z, N) \;=\;&
  \underbrace{E_{0,\beta} \cdot \big(T_1^{\rm free} - T_1^{\rm atom}\big)}_{\text{T1 binding}}
  \;+\;
  \underbrace{\alpha \cdot \big((T_2 + T_3)^{\rm atom} - (T_2 + T_3)^{\rm free}\big)}_{\text{T2/T3 binding}}
  \\[2pt]
  &+\;
  \underbrace{m_e \cdot \big(T_4^{\rm atom} - T_4^{\rm free}\big)}_{\text{T4 binding}}
  \;+\;
  \underbrace{E_{0,\beta} \cdot (a_K - 1) \cdot T_1^{\rm atom}}_{\text{T5 binding}}

  \underbrace{\big(T_6^{\rm atom} - T_6^{\rm free}\big)}_{\text{T6 binding}}

The scale difference separating T_1 from T_2+T_3 isolates the weak scale from the hadronic core.

prop:chirality-dual-space-derivation:
Proposition Chirality a_K = \prod_{pn} (1 + \mathrm{sign}\cdot h) from symmetric-channel trace duality. The chirality factor a_K derives exactly from the symmetric-channel trace structure of the H_3(q) Hecke generators. For every mixed \mathrm{pn} crossing c in the braid:

  a_K \;=\; \prod_{\substack{\text{pn crossings}\\ c \in \mathcal{B}_K}}
  \bigl(1 + \mathrm{sign}(c) \cdot h\bigr),
  \qquad
  h \;=\; q - q^{-1}.

This factorizes explicitly into the dual-space asymmetry of the Wedderburn channels:

  1 + \mathrm{sign}(c)\cdot h
  \;=\;
  1 \;+\; \mathrm{sign}(c) \cdot \bigl[\tau_{\mathrm{sym}}(\sigma) - \tau_{\mathrm{sym}}(\sigma^{-1})\bigr].

The identity requires no external phenomenological fitting. The symmetric channel is uniquely selected because it restricts to the trivial trace at q=1. This precisely identifies the "chirality content" as the deviation from involutive crossing behavior encoded in h. All six paper assignments match this formula.

rem:six-term-per-derivation-weights-argu:
Remark Argument for the six-term per-derivation weights (not a proof). Argument (not a proof). The constituent baseline Z\,m_{\mathfrak{p}} + N\,m_{\mathfrak{n}} + Z\,m_e is the free-particle sum. The binding energy is the algebraic difference of the bound atom's mass formula and its free baseline. Each of the six terms contributes additively to the categorical mass per unified six-term decomposition; isolating the physical scale of each contribution is exactly the per-derivation reading above:

  • T_1 binding (descended Markov): the categorical mass formula \mathfrak{m}(Z, N) = E_{0,\beta} \cdot \mathfrak{m}(\beta_{Z,N}) with E_{0,\beta} the β-decay scale per categorical mass, Markov reads T_1 in cat units. The binding contribution is the bound–free differential.
  • T_2 + T_3 binding (brane tower): per the atomic-braid mass formula in the Particles chapter, the binding correction is \alpha \cdot \sum_i \ln\lvert \hat V_i \rvert where \alpha = m_e \cdot 8G is the Borromean–Catalan binding scale (itself a conjecture) and G \approx 0.9160 is Catalan's constant. Per the mass-endomorphism tower, \alpha\,\ln\lvert V \rvert is the leading-order expansion of -\alpha\,\mathrm{Li}_2^q(-\lvert V \rvert), so the same \alpha scale governs both the leading-order and the corrected q-dilogarithm form.
  • T_4 binding (Frobenius co-Casimir): the universal Frobenius co-Casimir T_4 = m_e \cdot \sum_{\lambda \vdash 3A} 1/\dim_q(\lambda), a formal sum over all partitions, has m_e baked into the formula. At z = q^3/(q^2+1) this is not m_e \cdot \tau(C_{\dim_q}), since \tau(p_\lambda) = 0 on every block with three or more rows. Empirically the bound–free differential vanishes for the atomic-braid \tau, so T_4 contributes no binding at this stage (open question — see remarks).
  • T_5 binding (chirality): per chirality dual-space derivation, T_5 = (a_K - 1) \cdot T_1 as a multiplicative correction on T_1. With T_1 in cat units and E_{0,\beta} as T_1's MeV scale, the binding contribution is E_{0,\beta} \cdot (a_K - 1) \cdot T_1^{\rm atom}.
  • T_6 binding (cyclotomic tail): per full pole structure, T_6 comes pre-converted to MeV via the canonical Habiro residue evaluation. No additional scaling needed.

The total B(Z, N) is the sum of these per-term contributions and is positive for bound systems. The argument assumes the scale assignment of each term; it does not derive it, and the Catalan scale it uses is itself conjectural.

Comparison boundary. The measured inputs enter here and only here.

The assembly is implemented in the formal derivation as assemble_per_derivation_weights(Z, N) with hardcoded constants E_{0,\beta} = 0.78233341 MeV (CODATA β-decay Q), \alpha = m_e \cdot 8G = 3.74446989 MeV, m_e = 0.510999\;\text{MeV} MeV. Across the proton..{}^{9}Be spectrum (12 atoms):

These percentages are relative to the total atomic mass, whose constituent baseline Z\,m_{\mathfrak{p}} + N\,m_{\mathfrak{n}} + Z\,m_e is taken from CODATA, so they measure the binding only weakly. The comparison with the standalone atomic-braid formula (0.13–0.16% mean) and with the single-E_0 assembly (14.7% mean) is likewise a comparison on total mass, not on binding.

Open questions.

  1. T_4 binding contribution vanishes empirically. The evaluation of T_4 gives the same value for bound and free configurations, so the differential T_4^{\rm atom} - T_4^{\rm free} = 0 identically. Either T_4 is independent of inter-nucleon crossings by construction (in which case it cancels out of the binding formula and contributes only to the total mass via the Z\,m_{\mathfrak{p}} baseline), or the implementation is missing a coupling. Investigation pending.
  2. T_6 Habiro residue witness coverage. The _load_canonical_t6_MeV helper currently returns 0 for A \geq 5 atoms because the Habiro residue witness lacks data for them. Once populated, T_6 will start contributing to the heavier-atom predictions; expect {\sim}\,few-keV-level corrections per atom based on the A \leq 4 pattern.

prop:crystal-isospin-degeneracy:
Proposition Crystal-limit isospin degeneracy: S_{\mathrm{crystal}} is invariant under \sigma_i \leftrightarrow \sigma_i^{-1}. Let \beta_A be an atomic braid expressed as a finite word of signed generators \sigma_i^{\pm 1}. Inverting the sign of any subset of generators leaves the crystal-limit shell-correction sum invariant:

  S_{\mathrm{crystal}}(\beta_A) \;=\; S_{\mathrm{crystal}}(\beta_A').

The crystal limit q \to 0 completely masks generator inversions. It cannot distinguish between proton and neutron structures inside the crystal model. This is a property of the model, which sets the q = 0 actions of \sigma_i and \sigma_i^{-1} equal by definition; it is not a property of the Hecke algebra H_n(q), where \sigma_i and \sigma_i^{-1} have different eigenvalues. Any non-zero mass splitting between isospin mirrors, such as ^3\mathrm{H} and ^3\mathrm{He}, must originate strictly outside the crystal limit or via an asymmetric interface protocol.
prf:crystal-isospin-degeneracy:
Proof Proof of crystal isospin degeneracy. The crystal-limit character \chi^\lambda_{\mathrm{crystal}}(\sigma) on a single Hecke generator \sigma is, by crystal-graph realisation, the trace of the signed-permutation action

  \sigma_i : T \;\longmapsto\; \mathrm{sign}(\rho_T(i)) \cdot T,
  \qquad \rho_T(i) := c(T(i+1)) - c(T(i))

on the standard-Young-tableaux basis \mathrm{SYT}(\lambda), where c(\cdot) is the cell content (content scaling). The crystal model takes \sigma_i^{-1} to act by the same sign on the same line:

  \sigma_i^{-1} : T \;\longmapsto\; \mathrm{sign}(\rho_T(i)) \cdot T
  \;=\; \sigma_i \cdot T

acting on the same SYT eigenline. This is an input of the model (the \lvert i\rvert reduction in the crystal computation), not a consequence of the Hecke relation. The relation (\sigma_i - q)(\sigma_i + q^{-1}) = 0 cannot be specialised at q = 0, because q^{-1} is undefined there. At generic q it gives \sigma_i^{-1} = \sigma_i - (q - q^{-1}), so \sigma_i has eigenvalues q, -q^{-1} while \sigma_i^{-1} has q^{-1}, -q; the two are not equal on any line. In the seminormal form \sigma_i is also not diagonal on the SYT basis: it mixes T with s_i T whenever i and i+1 lie in different rows and columns of T. The crystal-limit generators therefore act diagonally on the SYT basis with eigenvalues that are individually invariant under \sigma_i \leftrightarrow \sigma_i^{-1}. For any fixed T \in \mathrm{SYT}(\lambda), the eigenvalue product along a braid word

  \mu^\lambda_T(\beta) \;:=\; \prod_{\ell \,\in\, \beta} \mathrm{eigval}_T(\ell)

is therefore equal under \beta \to \beta'. Note that \mu^\lambda_T is not the character \chi^\lambda — it is the eigenvalue product on the line through T; the character is the trace

  \chi^\lambda_{\mathrm{crystal}}(\beta) \;=\; \sum_{T \in \mathrm{SYT}(\lambda)}
      \mu^\lambda_T(\beta).

The trace is not multiplicative in \beta, but it is a sum of sign-flip-invariant per-eigenline contributions, so

  \chi^\lambda_{\mathrm{crystal}}(\beta_A)
    \;=\; \sum_{T \in \mathrm{SYT}(\lambda)} \mu^\lambda_T(\beta_A)
    \;=\; \sum_{T \in \mathrm{SYT}(\lambda)} \mu^\lambda_T(\beta_A')
    \;=\; \chi^\lambda_{\mathrm{crystal}}(\beta_A')

per partition. Summing against the (sign-independent) Plancherel weight w_\lambda(q = 1) = (f^\lambda)^2 / (3A)! yields the claim. \square

Conditional corollary (legacy disjoint-product convention). Suppose tritium and helium-3 are presented by the simplified disjoint-product words used by the canonical formalism

  \tilde\beta_T = \sigma_1\sigma_2\sigma_1^{-1}\sigma_4\sigma_5^{-1}\sigma_4
              \sigma_7\sigma_8^{-1}\sigma_7,
  \qquad
  \tilde\beta_{{}^3\mathrm{He}} = \sigma_1\sigma_2\sigma_1^{-1}\sigma_4\sigma_5\sigma_4^{-1}
              \sigma_7\sigma_8^{-1}\sigma_7

(differing only at positions 5 and 6 by paired inversion). Then

  S_{\mathrm{crystal}}(\tilde\beta_T) \;=\; S_{\mathrm{crystal}}(\tilde\beta_{{}^3\mathrm{He}}),

matching the recorded crystal computation which records both values to fifty decimal digits as 0.0020612874779541296.

Caveat — this corollary is not a statement about physical {}^3\mathrm{H} vs. {}^3\mathrm{He}. Under the canonical \bowtie_K-coupled convention the canonical formalism, {}^3\mathrm{H} has interface types (pn{=}\bowtie_K,\;nn{=}\sigma^{-1}) while {}^3\mathrm{He} has (pp{=}\sigma,\;pn{=}\bowtie_K) — the words differ in interface type, not just generator signs, so the sign-flip proposition does not apply directly. The legacy disjoint-product computation artificially erases this isospin asymmetry.

The knot topology dictates the mass scale through this coupling.
prop:meson-kaon-pion-hecke-seifert:

  \frac{\mathfrak{m}_K}{\mathfrak{m}_\pi}

  \chi^{(2,1)}(\sigma_1^5)
  \;\times\;
  \biggl(\frac{V_S(T(2,5))}{V_S(T(2,3))}\biggr)^{\!2}.
